result:
Clean. Here's a summary of what I did and why.

## Root cause

GSC showed a huge gap: the homepage ranks fine (pos 4.5) but every blog post — despite genuinely good, relevant content — sits at position 42-58 with near-zero clicks, even on high-impression terms like "inbox zero method" (3,900 impressions) and "gmail storage full." Investigating the live site and source explained why: the SaaS pivoted from **Lumina** (AI meeting assistant) to **InboxZap** (email cleanup app), but the pivot was never finished:

- Nav, homepage copy, footer, and JSON-LD still said "Lumina" / AI meeting assistant, while the blog content was already 100% about email cleanup — a glaring entity/topic mismatch for both users and crawlers.
- The blog index fetched `/api/posts`, which doesn't exist (404) — so the blog had **zero internal links to any post**. They were orphaned pages.
- The sitemap explicitly excluded blog posts (a `TODO` comment).
- Three separate posts (`post-3`, `post-7`, `post-12`) all targeted "bulk delete emails" — keyword cannibalization splitting authority three ways.
- `/features`, `/pricing` were linked in nav but didn't exist in source; `/faq` redirected to a `#faq` anchor that didn't exist on the homepage.
- Post slugs (`/blog/post-1`) and titles ("...in 2024") carried no keyword or freshness signal.

## What I fixed (verified with a real `next build` + `next start`)

- Finished the rebrand: homepage, nav, footer, and schema now consistently say InboxZap.
- Converted the blog to real server-rendered pages (`app/blog/posts.ts`, `app/blog/page.tsx`, `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`) with proper metadata, canonicals, OG tags, and `BlogPosting` JSON-LD — no more dependence on a dead API.
- Merged the three cannibalizing "bulk delete" posts into one authoritative guide; gave all 12 old `post-N` slugs descriptive, keyword-rich names with 301 redirects so the GSC-tracked URLs don't just disappear.
- Fixed `sitemap.ts` to include all 10 posts.
- Built the missing `/features` and `/pricing` pages, and a real `#faq` section with `FAQPage` JSON-LD.
- Added `Organization`/`SoftwareApplication` JSON-LD and a `public/llms.txt` for AI-answer-engine visibility.

One unrelated thing worth flagging: `npm install` warned that `next@14.2.5` has a known security vulnerability with a patch available — not an SEO fix, but worth upgrading separately since a compromised site is bad for traffic too.
